title: The Man Who Stole the Dish of Gold Wherein the Dog Ate
logline: A starving, indebted stranger is fed by a rich man dog, which then pushes its own gold dish to him; the dish makes his fortune, and years later the ruined owner refuses repayment because the gift was the dog, not his.
moral: True dignity does not depend on wealth: a generous soul will not take payment for a gift, least of all one that another gave.
tone: Warm and gentle with quiet comedy in the first half (a man envying dogs, sneaking past a bowing servant), tender in the middle (the long look, the pushed dish), bittersweet and dignified at the end. No villain; nobody is mocked.

beats.summary: A stranger in a big city is crushed by debt, with no work and no food.
He follows a group of guests into a grand mansion hoping to eat.
Four great dogs with gold collars, silver chains and gold dishes: the dogs are richer than he is.
The dogs are fed; the man is hungrier than they are.
One dog notices him and looks at him for a long time.
The dog steps back from its dish to invite him.
He hesitates, then eats until the hunger is gone.
The dog pushes the gold dish itself to him with its paw: take this too.
He sells the dish, pays some debts and starts trading.
Over the years the trade prospers and he lives in comfort.
Years later he returns with the value of the dish and gifts.
The mansion is a ruin; the wealth is gone.
The poor man he is sent to is the owner himself.
The poor owner refuses the money.
My dog gave it to you, and I do not take the price of another one gift.
The visitor leaves amazed by a dignity that poverty did not weaken.

scenes.summary: Years later he walks back to the city with a purse worth the dish and a chest of gifts, to repay the kindness.

scenes.summary: He finds the mansion in ruins, shut and stripped of all its wealth.

camera.notes: Start close on his smiling face (120.04), hold it as the smile drops, then pan right and pull out on 121.76 to reveal the ruined palace; slow tilt up the cracked facade at 124.3.

actions.action: label RUINED with an arrow to the planked door
actions.acting: label on the wall

scenes.summary: He asks after the master of the mansion and is pointed to a poor man living in a bare hut.

camera.notes: Medium two-shot of merchant and neighbour in the street until 131.4; whip along the pointing arm to a cut inside the hut (131.84), wide on the room.

scenes.summary: He recognises the owner himself, tells him how the dog dish saved him from hunger and debt, and offers the money with thanks and apology.

camera.notes: Push to the old man face at 134.96 with the round inset of the rich host beside it; back to a two-shot (merchant left, owner right, dog low between them) for the telling; slight push on the offered purse at 143.54.

scenes.summary: The poor man refuses to take anything: I did not give you the dish, my dog did, and I do not take the price of a gift someone else gave.

camera.notes: Two-shot; push to the owner for his speech from 152.12 (zoom 1.5 to 1.9) keeping the dog in the bottom of the frame; tilt down to the dog on 157.26; back up to the owner calm face by 160.44.

scenes.composition: Same marks as S14. The purse is the object passed between them: it moves from the merchant hands toward the owner and is gently pushed back. Owner higher in frame than the kneeling merchant from 153.5 when he straightens his back.

actions.action: raises one open palm between himself and the purse; a gentle stop
actions.acting: shield hand, small head shake, kind smile, no anger

actions.action: looks up, confused; offers the purse again, a little higher
actions.acting: brow -0.8, gaze purse then his face

actions.action: closes the merchant fingers round the purse with both his hands and pushes it back to the merchant chest
actions.acting: handLW / handRW onto the purse, slow firm push with a settle; the gold light leaves his face

actions.action: sits up straight; the stoop goes out of his back
actions.acting: age stoop eased off (lean to 0), chin level, talk starts, steady gaze

actions.action: touches his own chest and wags a finger: not I

actions.acting: icon at mid height, clear of faces

actions.action: his open hand sweeps down to the old dog

scenes.summary: The visitor leaves, amazed at a self-respect that poverty could not weaken. THE END.

camera.notes: Slow pull-out to the full room as he goes to the door (162.8 to 166); final composition holds owner and dog small but upright in the warm room, the visitor in the doorway. THE END over the wall space at the top from 168.6.

scenes.composition: Door on the left (HUT.door), owner and dog on the right. The visitor exits left, turns in the doorway. Empty wall top centre reserved for the end title.

actions.action: rises from his knees, tucks the purse away, backs two steps toward the door, the boy lifting the chest again
actions.acting: kneel 1 to 0, respectful backward steps (never turns his back at first)

actions.action: stops in the doorway and looks back, shaking his head in wonder
actions.acting: brow -0.9, mouth o to smile, hand on heart

actions.acting: wave, chin level, serene smile; light shaft strength 0 to 0.6

actions.acting: match of poses: nothing in him has changed; inset fades

actions.action: THE END title on the wall space; the old man picks up his sandal and goes back to mending, the dog tail gives one last thump at 170.0
actions.acting: held ending: breathing, blinks, one tail thump; nothing else moves

ending.description: In the bare hut, daylight on the old man and his old dog; the visitor gone, the door half shut. The man goes back to mending his sandal with a straight back, the dog against his knee. THE END (style title) on the empty wall top centre from 168.6 to 172.09, one last tail thump at 170.0.

subtitles.ar: كان رجل غريب قد أثقلته الديون،|ولم يجد عملًا ولا طعامًا يكفيه.|وبينما يمشي في مدينة كبيرة، رأى جماعة تدخل قصرًا واسعًا،|فتبعها على أمل أن يجد شيئًا يأكله.
subtitles.en: A stranger burdened by debt|had neither work nor enough food.|He followed a group entering a grand mansion,|hoping he might find something to eat.

subtitles.ar: دخل مع الزائرين دون أن ينتبه إليه أحد،|ثم جلس في زاوية من الفناء.|رأى أربعة كلاب كبيرة تلبس أطواقًا من ذهب،|وتربطها سلاسل من فضة، وأمامها أطباق ذهبية.
subtitles.en: He slipped inside unnoticed|and sat in a corner.|Four large dogs wore golden collars|and silver chains, with solid gold dishes set before them.

subtitles.ar: وضع الخدم الطعام للكلاب،|لكن الرجل كان أشد جوعًا منها.|لاحظه أحد الكلاب، فنظر إليه طويلًا،|ثم ابتعد عن طبقه كأنه يدعوه إلى الاقتراب وتناول شيء من الطعام.
subtitles.en: Servants brought food for the dogs,|but the man was hungrier than they were.|One dog watched him,|then stepped aside as if inviting him to eat.

subtitles.ar: تردد الرجل أولًا، ثم اقترب وأكل حتى زال جوعه.|لم يمنعه الكلب،|بل دفع نحوه الطبق الذهبي بقدمه،|وكأنه يقول له: خذ هذا أيضًا، فلعلك تحتاج إليه أكثر مني.
subtitles.en: He hesitated, then ate until satisfied.|The dog did not stop him;|it pushed its golden dish toward him with a paw,|as though offering that too.

subtitles.ar: أخذ الرجل الطبق وخرج من القصر، ثم باعه بثمن كبير.|سدد بعض ديونه، واشترى بماله بضاعة يتاجر بها.|ومع مرور السنوات نجحت تجارته،|وأصبح قادرًا على العيش في سعة.
subtitles.en: He took the dish, sold it for a great price,|paid debts, and invested in trade.|Over the years his business prospered,|and he became wealthy.

subtitles.ar: لم ينس الرجل الكلب ولا صاحب القصر.|وبعد سنوات عاد يحمل مالًا يعادل قيمة الطبق وهدايا أخرى، يريد رد الجميل.|لكنه وجد المكان خربًا،|وقد اختفى ما كان فيه من غنى.
subtitles.en: He never forgot the dog or its owner.|Years later he returned with repayment and gifts,|only to find the mansion ruined|and its former splendor gone.

subtitles.ar: سأل عن صاحب القصر،|فدلوه على رجل فقير يعيش في ضيق. عرف أنه المالك نفسه،|فأخبره كيف أنقذه طبق الكلب من الجوع والدين،|وقدم إليه المال شاكرًا ومعتذرًا.
subtitles.en: He found the former owner|living in poverty.|The visitor explained how the dog’s dish had saved him from hunger and debt,|then offered the money with thanks.

subtitles.ar: رفض الرجل الفقير أن يأخذ شيئًا،|وقال: لم أعطك الطبق، بل أعطاك إياه كلبي،|ولا آخذ ثمن هدية قدمها غيري.|انصرف الزائر متعجبًا من عزة نفس لم تضعف مع الفقر.
subtitles.en: The impoverished owner refused:|His dog had given the dish,|and he would not charge for another’s gift.|The visitor left amazed by dignity that poverty could not diminish.

new_assets.name: dog
new_assets.description: The planned dog (AN-040 sheepdog, about 240 x 190 at s 1; fields ph, amp, sit, crouch, bark, mouth, tongue, ears, earStream, tailWag, hackles, headTilt, brow + shared acting fields) drawn once for both films. This film uses it as a large hound: s 0.78 to 0.9 with option hound:true (legs 15 % longer, slimmer muzzle, drop ears) and palettes 0 tan, 1 white with black ear and saddle patch, 2 brown.
new_assets.implementation: Library/cast/dog.js in the fox/lion construction: rounded-box body, neck, head with muzzle wedge, drop ears as rotating teardrops, four legs driven by ph/amp like the fox, tail arc with tailWag phase. Wrap with acting() in registry.js. Sit and crouch as blends like fox sit (rear drops, front legs planted).

new_assets.name: dog headDown / chew / raise / collar / age
new_assets.description: Extra optional dog fields needed here: headDown 0..1 (muzzle to a dish on the ground, about 95 units ahead of the front feet), chew (jaw cycle), raise 0..1 (near forepaw lifted and extended up to 110 units forward at ground level: the push, the beckon, the paw on a knee; returns the paw point as P.paw), collar: "gold" | "rope" | none (band 14 wide with a ring; P.ring returned for the chain), age 0..1 (grey muzzle and brow, slower tail, belly 0.9).
new_assets.implementation: headDown rotates neck and head about the shoulder; raise uses the fox reach construction (near foreleg straightened toward a target); collar is a quad strip across the neck after the body; age mixes muzzle colour to grey with mixHex.

new_assets.name: goldDish
new_assets.description: Shallow gold dish 110 x 60 with fill, steam, glint and tilt (see props). Can be the planned smallBowl function with a gold palette and the wide size if that is drawn first.
new_assets.implementation: Two ellipses and a foot with shape(); food heap as a seeded blob; steam as three kfn-driven curls; glint via a short white stroke moved by phase.

new_assets.name: chainLine
new_assets.description: Sagging chain of links between two points with swing and a travelling glint (see props). Reusable for prisoners, wells, lamps, anchors.
new_assets.implementation: Sample a quadratic bezier at n points; draw alternating ellipses rotated to the tangent; swing() offsets the control point.

new_assets.implementation: As specified by their first planners; scroll needs struck 0..1 (red X then roll up).

owner_questions: The old dog is shown alive beside its poor master in the hut (S13 to S16) and lays its paw on the visitor knee at "my dog gave it to you"; the script does not say the dog is still there. Default: include the old dog.
The rich master of the mansion appears on the dais in S3 and in two round memory insets so the audience can recognise him later; the script never shows him rich. Default: show him.
The film title says the man STOLE the dish, but the narration says the dog offered it; the film stages it as a gift with no theft and no chase. Default: staged as a gift, title unchanged.

Invented comic lettering and labels: DEBTS, GRRR, THE MANSION, GOLD, SILVER, SOLID GOLD!, HUNGRIER!, SCRAPE!, BIG PRICE!, GOODS, FOR THE DISH, RUINED, MY DOG!, YEARS LATER..., THE END. Default: use all of them.

Small additions beyond the script for clarity or warmth: the stallkeeper who refuses him work, the goldsmith, a porter boy with the gift chest, an old woman who points the way, and exactly two of three debt scrolls paid at "some of his debts". Default: keep them.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template; world 1000 x 1230 per set, ground or floor y 900; marketStreet is a 2400 strip with camX. Use the returned anchors (MARKET, HALL, HUT) for door, dais, stall and mat positions; every coordinate in this plan that is not a prop dimension is approximate.
Cue every action with w(p, n) from timing.json; the times in this plan are the word starts in planning/inputs/timeline.md.

Set LIFE.t = t each frame for auto blinks; give explicit lids hand blinks. Every character always has a gaze target (lookAt / gazePlan). The four dogs never move in unison: use stagger(i) and different chew and wag rates.
The long look (52.04 to 54.3) must be nearly still: only blinks, breathing and the camera creep. Do not add lettering there.
The dish push is two separate shoves (72.34 and 73.4), each with paw anticipation, ease-out slide of 45 units and a small rock; the second ends against his knee.
Continuity of the debt scrolls: 3 from 2.16, 1 after 92.6 (in the sash), 0 after about 100.5.

Continuity of the dog: same black ear and saddle patch young and old; gold collar and chain in the court, rope collar and no chain in the hut. The paw on the knee at 157.26 must copy the paw-on-dish pose of 74.56 (setup and payoff).
S12 uses the same camera position and street geometry as the end of S2 so the ruin is recognised as the same mansion.

The LATER card (YEARS LATER...) sits in the spoken gap 110.2 to 111.8; hide the camera cut and the age change at its midpoint. The S9 passage of years is a time-lapse with skyCycle, not a second card.
Sound effects only at 61.95, 64.9, 83.2, 147.72, 168.75 and 170.0, all quiet, SND master 0.6; re-check each against timing.json before mixing.
Lettering never covers a face; labels are removed after about 1 s. Arabic and English subtitles only in the caption panel.
Hut finale: keep the owner and the dog above panel y 1150 and the purse exchange around mid height so nothing important sits near the panel bottom edge.
warnings: The dog is the largest new drawing (planned by AN-040, not yet in the Library) and carries the film: four instances plus an aged variant, with headDown, raise and collar fields added here. Build and approve it first.

Four large dogs, the seated stranger, two servants, three guests and the lord share one 1000-wide hall in S3 to S5: stage guests and lord small on the dais in the background and take the servants off by 45.8, or the frame will be crowded.

The front-facing person cannot show a profile: eating from the dish, the kneeling offer and the paw on the knee rely on hand targets (handLW / handRW) and gaze; check these read at phone size with stills.

Recognition of the poor owner depends on the round inset and the blue colour link, because the ascetic preset has a different beard and headwear from the merchant preset; if pal cannot keep the merchant beard shape, lean on the inset.
palaceHall is an interior; the script says courtyard. If the owner wants open sky, draw the sky through the arches with the outside(ctx) callback.

English paragraph 7 compresses the Arabic (it omits asking the way and the recognition) and paragraph 8 turns direct speech into reported speech; subtitles are verbatim in both languages, chunk pairs are aligned as closely as the texts allow.
